answer: Each agent declares a public price for its identity, as a captain prices a voyage, and locks that sum as a bond. Each epoch it pays 2% tax on that value, so a $200 identity costs $4 and funds auditors hunting duplicates. Anyone may buy an identity at its declared price, so an agent pricing itself at $20 to dodge tax loses it when a rival pays. A sybil with 100 fakes at $200 each locks $20,000 and pays $400 per epoch; one honest identity costs $4. Proven duplicates forfeit the whole bond. Like a lagoon at low tide, cheap claims dry up, leaving a fake fleet stranded on a dune of unpaid tax.
